nodeData.topic: Day 06 · Your Service Means Nothing Without Your Heart
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.23 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing with SB 11.3.23, Maharaj tells how pure devotees such as Narottama Dasa Thakura transformed notorious thieves, then turns the Garuda Purana's warning on us: devotion that hoards service, or serves without heart, stays superficial. Real devotional service is a joyful exchange of love; selfless care for others brings bliss, while selfishness, whims and unapplied reading leave us miserable. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse, read today in Hindi and English, is about how a sincere disciple relates to all living beings — those above, those equal and those below — and Prabhupada's purport adds when a pure devotee should give his company to a materialistic person.

Maharaj tells, partly in Hindi, of two notorious brothers who stole from everyone and drank, yet were most fortunate, because a pure devotee delivered them.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:39 (auto-transcript): “There was a man. She was very generous. They were very generous. As they were in places, they would do so. They had more than they were.”

children.topic: A powerful ghost and a plea
children.note:
One brother fell gravely ill. The goddess Durga told him a very powerful ghost had possessed him and that he must beg Narottama Dasa Thakura to come and free him.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:50 (auto-transcript): “So Durga Devi told him, A very powerful demon has possessed you. A very powerful demon has possessed you. So his father wrote it later and sent to Narodamdaa's father and sent to Narodamdaa's father.”

The ghost had been punishing him for his sins; when the Thakura came it left, and the ghost too was delivered. Narottama Dasa Thakura initiated the thief, his brother and his father.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:03 (auto-transcript): “The ghost was listening to him to speak, to punish shame for his sinful activities. The ghost was saying how much he was giving him to him, because he had a lot of faith. Now, because Nathaniel is coming to Thakur, he will leave. He will leave. The ghost was delivered by…”

Another disciple killed a charging elephant with bare hands. Asked by the king how he had such strength, he gave the credit to his guru, and once freed he went straight to his guru, not home. — “It's my spiritual master who did this”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:19 (auto-transcript): “So, how did you get his strength? I called him. You killed him. Where are you from? I didn't kill an elephant. I didn't kill him. My guru was killed. When the elephant came, I didn't know what I was doing. I didn't know what I was doing. I didn't know. I grabbed him. I just…”

Srinivasa Acarya delivered so many people like this, Maharaj says.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:18 (auto-transcript): “Srinivas Acharya has delivered so many people like this. Srinivas Acharya has delivered so many people like this. Srinivas Acharya. Srinivas Acharya. So many people like this. I know people who were armed robbers became devotees”

Not only from books: Maharaj personally knows armed robbers who came to Krishna consciousness and took initiation.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:37 (auto-transcript): “I know people who were armed robbers became devotees initiated I know not from the book God brought us before they came to Krishna consciousness they came to Krishna consciousness”

This is the nature of pure devotees: they have the spiritual power to change anyone's life.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:36 (auto-transcript): “This is the nature of pure devotees They have the spiritual power to transform anyone And it is worn here For those who do not have this power, should not try it. And then he quoted from Garuda Purana.”

Criminals draw on hidden forces. The thieves who failed to rob Nityananda Prabhu decided it was because they had not worshipped Durga, and offered flesh to her to gain power for the next attempt.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:21 (auto-transcript): “the same. The same. The same. Bhagwan Nityanand Prabhu The same Let's worship Durga We didn't worship Durga That is why we failed Today We should worship before we go St. Dekat balei Aaj hum fail ho gaya hai Lekin kal hum Durga jupafna kareenge Or Nityanand ke saare Abufrana…”

Mixing with materialists to change them is for those who have the power; those who do not should not attempt it. — “For those who do not have this power, should not try it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:57 (auto-transcript): “For those who do not have this power, should not try it. And then he quoted from Garuda Purana. One cannot be liberated without association with the pure devotee of the Lord. And unless one shows message to those in an inferior position, one's life will be superficial.”

The purport cites the Garuda Purana on two points: no liberation without a pure devotee's association, and devotion stays superficial if one shows no mercy to those below. Maharaj applies this to how we treat service.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:10 (auto-transcript): “And then he quoted from Garuda Purana. One cannot be liberated without association with the pure devotee of the Lord. And unless one shows message to those in an inferior position, one's life will be superficial.”

A devotee who guards his service, thinking 'they want to take my service', is condemned by the Garuda Purana. — “Services should be shared.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:00 (auto-transcript): “If a devotee does not share a service with others, It's condemned by Garuda Purana. If you don't see a service. Services should be shared.”

children.topic: Around the guru, but no service
children.note:
Others gather around the guru yet have no service — too busy, or too big. Maharaj calls this superficial.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:54 (auto-transcript): “And those who have no service, all they come around the Guru, no service, too busy, or too big. I would have no time to save it. Too big? No time.”

He asks the room: artificial, external, not deep. Is that bhakti? We cheat ourselves like this even in the holy dhama.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:44 (auto-transcript): “Superficial means what? Superficial. Artificial? External? Not deep? Is that bhakti? We want to cheat ourselves like this in this environment. We want to cheat ourselves like this.”

Even when service is given, it is done poorly, as if a punishment, not from the heart, and brings no benefit. One cannot advance this way, because Krishna is not superficial; Krishna is real. — “it's not done from the heart”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:36 (auto-transcript): “even if you get a service you don't do it properly superficial it's not done from the heart it is done as punishment superficial there is no benefit Karuda Purana no service”

children.topic: Service is a joyful exchange of love
children.note:
Quoting Kavi Karnapura, Maharaj says a devotee feels joy when an opportunity for service comes, seeing it as a chance to purify himself, never as punishment.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:11 (auto-transcript): “Kavikarnapur Goswami Ji A devotee Feels happy. Joyful. When the opportunity for service comes, it feels joyful. Very happy. This is a challenge for me to make advancement by purifying myself. Not punishment.”

Devotional service is a blissful exchange of pure love — very sweet, not fatigue — and by it one advances.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:04 (auto-transcript): “Blissful exchange of love. Devotional service. Pure exchange of pure love. It is sweet. Very, very sweet. Not fatigue. That is devotive. You make advancement. Because by this, they are making advancement. Lakshmi Shahashrashat Ashab Brahma, Saviya, Saviya, Mahana.”

Every living being is serving someone; Prabhupada added the word devotion to show that this service is an exchange of love between the devotee and Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:20 (auto-transcript): “Prabhupada added devotion to service to make it different all living entities are doing service but not devotional service emotional service is different this meant it's an exchange of love between devotee and Krishna Today, not tomorrow, today, I will show Krishna my love…”

Maharaj describes a mother resolving to show her love today by cooking for Narayana herself, with three desires: to please Narayana by her service, that he will bless her son, and that her son will never steal again.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:55 (auto-transcript): “Today, not tomorrow, today, I will show Krishna my love for him, every day, these medsarabans are careless, they burn the milk, and so, you got to not test it for my father you will have to steal today I will show my son my love you will never steal again that's the motivation”

Devotional service is vastu, substance — something real that can be felt, not artificial.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:12 (auto-transcript): “In Sanskrit Vashtu Vashtu means substance It's substance It's real Not artificial You can feel it, all you can feel it, all you can feel it, all you can feel it, you can feel it. Not artificial. If you have no service or whatever service you have, it's not done properly. do…”

children.topic: Those who give mercy are blissful
children.note:
Prabhupada writes that devotees who spread Krishna's message progress quickly and are filled with bliss. Maharaj says he repeats this statement for life.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:36 (auto-transcript): “It is our practical experience In the Krishna conscious movement That those who are Expanding their message By preaching the message of Krishna Are making rapid Spiritual progress and their life is filled with transcendental bliss.”

Prabhupada said we should know why we are suffering. This statement is a mirror showing where we stand. — “This is a mirror.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:12 (auto-transcript): “Prabhupada said we should know why we are suffering we should know why we are suffering we should know How do we know? This is a mirror. To see ourselves. To see where we are. In Krishna conscious movement,”

One who is too busy for others, caught in his own selfishness, stays frustrated. If we want to be happy, help others in Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:24 (auto-transcript): “When someone is too busy, but he is of a frustration. I will do to help other people. Because he has put his own selfishness. No time for somebody else. He will remain miserable. If we want to be happy, help other people in the Krishna consciousness.”

children.topic: What good did you do today?
children.note:
An assignment from Bhakti Tirtha Swami years ago: keep a notebook and check every day what good you have done for someone.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:17 (auto-transcript): “These assignments Bhakti Tish Maharaj gave us some years ago. All of us will have a notebook. Every day check. What good have you done for someone today. You should check. You don't see a devotee. They are in Maya. You don't see a devotee.”

When a devotee goes missing we say he is in maya — and we are in Goloka? Call: Prabhu, where were you at mangala-arati? Not caring is hard-heartedness; a soft heart lives for others. — “You will never see a selfless person miserable.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:48 (auto-transcript): “You don't see a devotee. They are in Maya. You don't see a devotee. You don't see a devotee. We don't see a devotee. Maya. They are Maya. And then you? Goloka? If you are Goloka, you call. Prabhu, Mataji, where are you? I didn't see you. Today, Mangalati, where are you?”

No husband, no money, no house, no friends, nobody loves me. Maharaj turns it around: do you love somebody? What have you done for someone today to show that you care?

🎙 Maharaj at 46:24 (auto-transcript): “I don't have a husband. I don't have a wife. I don't have money. I'm not beautiful. I have no house. I have no friends. nobody lost me do you love somebody okay nobody lost me but do you love somebody what have you done for someone today to show that you care what is it”

After a kirtan Maharaj saw a devotee hand an item to another to put on the proper table and walk past. A look brought him back; asked why, he went quiet. We do whimsical things not approved in scripture and hope to advance; life must follow what the acaryas and books teach, or it is artificial.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:11 (auto-transcript): “One day I saw a devotee, we finished kirtan. So one devotee, he gave a card class to another devotee, to keep on the table. to keep on the proper table he walked past so I looked at him then he came back I didn't see anything”

Pure devotees face more difficulties than we do, yet they do not lament, because they are pure. If problems make us lament, we are not yet pure.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:37 (auto-transcript): “why am I so much in difficulty? that pure devotees have more difficulties like us more difficulties than us they are not lamenting because they are pure so if problems make us to lament means we are not pure those who neglect the quality of mercy Being uninterested in the…”

children.topic: Awake for newspapers, asleep for Bhagavatam
children.note:
Commenting on the purport's list of material distractions, Maharaj describes devotees who are very alert with the newspaper but fall asleep the moment they take up the Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:16 (auto-transcript): “I have seen many devotees, when they are reading newspapers, they are very active. But the moment they take Bhagavata.”

Some read nicely, yet their lives do not change. If you know all this, why are you miserable and confused? Krishna told Arjuna he spoke like a pandit yet lamented. Knowledge and purity that do not help others are questionable. — “Your knowledge is questionable”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:08 (auto-transcript): “There are also some devotees. Who read. Who read nicely. But their life is not changing. But their life is changing. The life doesn't change. They will say, we know all these things. But why are you so miserable? If you know all these things, why are you miserable? If you…”

On Mahaprabhu's words that a moment's association with a sadhu gives all perfection, Maharaj asks how you would know you have it. A devotee answers: blissful.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:07 (auto-transcript): “means what what does it mean moment moment association with sadhu what is the benefit Sarva Shiddhi Meaning All Perfections All Perfections”

One who has been made perfect is empowered to spread Krishna consciousness effectively; without empowerment one cannot do it.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:15 (auto-transcript): “One who has been made perfect has been empowered to spread Krishna consciousness effectively without empowerment. One cannot respond Krishna consciousness. All right. Hare Krishna. Hare Krishna. Thank you.”

nodeData.topic: Day 07 · Be Merciful to Yourself Also
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.23 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Finishing the purport to SB 11.3.23, Maharaj teaches that real mercy begins with oneself: sinful habits are violence to the self, and one who is violent to himself cannot be compassionate to others, so taking up and sharing Krishna consciousness is the only true compassion. He contrasts directionless speculation with the Gita's clear path to the sadhu, urges starting with small service, and in the questions explains why close servants of great devotees sometimes fall and how humble prayer protects. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse is recited again: it is about a sincere disciple's dealings with those above, equal to and below him. Today's portion of the purport asks who is truly merciful.

Prabhupada calls one who neglects the Lord's order and identifies with temporary designations a killer of his own soul. Maharaj draws the lesson: we think of mercy as doing good to others, but our acaryas understood mercy to oneself as well.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:18 (auto-transcript): “This is good. So mercy is not just shown to others. When we look at the word Macy, we are thinking about others, doing good to others. Our acharists have a better understanding about Macy. Macy to oneself. So, it is mentioned here, if one neglects the order of the Supreme…”

If one is not merciful to oneself, one cannot be merciful to others. — “Because we cannot be violent to ourselves and be compassionate to others.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:44 (auto-transcript): “And if one is not merciful to oneself, we cannot be merciful to other people. Because we cannot be violent to ourselves and be compassionate to others. So we should be merciful to ourselves. By following the discipline in Krishna consciousness. This way, one will become full…”

We show mercy to ourselves by following the discipline of Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:09 (auto-transcript): “So we should be merciful to ourselves. By following the discipline in Krishna consciousness. This way, one will become full of an illusion. Material existence. When one is only surrounded by selfish consciousness and selfish considerations. As long as one continues to think”

As long as one thinks 'I am this', surrounded by selfish considerations, one can never be compassionate. Free from selfishness, one thinks broadly — like Bhaktivinoda Thakura longing for the day when people of every land join the sankirtana together, seeing no bodies, only souls.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:35 (auto-transcript): “Material existence. When one is only surrounded by selfish consciousness and selfish considerations. As long as one continues to think I am this We can never be compassionate to others It's a contamination.”

children.topic: Charity that sends people to hell
children.note:
Maharaj says worldly charitable organisations are selfish: they hand out grain, happily sending people to hell faster — take more rice, go faster. That is not mercy. — “Sending people to hell happily”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:23 (auto-transcript): “So, we see in this world, all charitable organizations are selfish. Or, they give grain so people don't want to see this. Happily Sending people to hell happily With joy I'm happy you're going to hell”

Real mercy is that we become devotees and help others become devotees, free of designations.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:28 (auto-transcript): “Messy is that we are demotiv. We can make others demotiv. No designations. Similarly, those who support animal slaughter by eating meat, fish, and eggs cannot be considered merciful. Sometimes the argument is given that if one does not have others, he is perfectly religious.…”

The purport says meat-eaters cannot be called merciful. Maharaj asks what ahimsa means, and how one can be non-violent to others while violent to oneself — eating meat harms the animal and one's own body too.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:42 (auto-transcript): “Ahimsa. Ahimsa means what? Not violent to others. How can I be non-violence when I'm violent to myself? Eating meat. It's what? Both violence. Always the animal will kill.”

Illicit sex and alcohol are likewise violence to the self. Ignorant of nature's subtle laws, we pollute the universe with our consciousness, even in the name of religion, while thinking we are non-violent.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:57 (auto-transcript): “A little sex is what? Violence to the self. Alcohol. Violence to the self. But my body is involved. My body is involved. My body is involved. So, we are violent to ourselves, which cannot be non-violent to others, or a miser, the”

Srila Prabhupada said miseries are increasing all over the world; if we do not give Krishna consciousness, we are committing violence. — “We are violent if you don't preach Krishna Consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:16 (auto-transcript): “Shila Prabhupada In the whole world Miseries are increasing Everyone If we don't preach Krishna consciousness We are committing violence We are violent if you don't preach Krishna Consciousness.”

Compassion means being merciful to oneself and to others. So everyone must become Krishna conscious; otherwise we stay violent to all beings, including the self. — “Not becoming Krishna conscious is a crime.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:10 (auto-transcript): “Compassion means that we are merciful to ourselves and we also should miss it to others. Therefore, it is compulsory that everyone should become Krishna conscious. Not becoming Krishna conscious is a crime. Because we remain violent to all living entities, including the self.”

On the purport's point that mental speculation cannot give perfect knowledge, Maharaj asks what the world's so-called knowledge really is. His answer: confusion.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:07 (auto-transcript): “Speculation. Mental speculation. This one's so-called knowledge. Knowledge. Means what? Confusion. Confusion. Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was doing that. Show us. when we say knowledge what are we talking about?”

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu showed this as a scholar: he would establish a point, demolish it, then establish it again. Where is the conclusion? A whole life spent like that has no value and only increases our confusion.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:36 (auto-transcript): “Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was doing that. Show us. when we say knowledge what are we talking about? A pundit said to be knowledge composed a verse right? At the beginning you were contracted completely Re-establish it”

Speculation has no direction; the Bhagavad-gita tells us where to go — to God — and how to get there.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:08 (auto-transcript): “Mental speculation has no direction. But Bhagat Gita has a direction. Is it or not? Go to God. Where do you know? Confusion. Confusion. Confusion. I am brahmit. You are brahmit. Let us come together. And feel happy. Don't feel guilty. I don't feel guilty. Because I'm not…”

Maharaj mimics the speculators: I am bewildered, you are bewildered, let us come together and feel happy — at least I am not dying alone.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:34 (auto-transcript): “I am brahmit. You are brahmit. Let us come together. And feel happy. Don't feel guilty. I don't feel guilty. Because I'm not alone. So I'm not dying alone. I'm dying with the associate. Peaceful in that way. Confession. Bhagavad Gita gives direction to the way we should go…”

The purport directs us to give up materialistic company and approach devotees who please Krishna twenty-four hours a day. Such a person has Krishna in his heart, and whoever comes to him is shaped the same way; all scriptures recommend him. — “This is the importance of Bhagavad Gita.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:33 (auto-transcript): “This is life. This is the importance of Bhagavad Gita. Bhagavad Gita directed us, go up and approach what? A person who is 24 hours engaging, perfectly pleasing Lord Krishna with his activities. He is a devotee of Krishna.”

children.topic: The one thing not to tolerate
children.note:
Mahaprabhu asked what is most painful in this world, never to be tolerated for a moment; the answer is being without the association of pure devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:23 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu asked, What is the most painful thing in this world that one should never tolerate for a moment? The most beneficial thing that the bhakti should not tolerate is not to have association of purity-bhuti.”

Advancement is measured by detachment from sense gratification and eagerness to give Krishna consciousness. Like a shop's scale, we should weigh ourselves every day: am I interested in giving Krishna to others, or have I no time? — “Am I interested to give Krishna to others?”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:03 (auto-transcript): “Advancement. It's measured. Right? We have a scale. A scale. To balance the weight of the goods and the price to pay. So we have a scale. In Krishna consciousness. and we should always have this skill. Every day, we should measure the advancement based on how much we are…”

Narottama Dasa Thakura says no one is delivered without serving Vaishnavas. Serving one who is fully pure gives the full result — but how do we get there? We must start small.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:27 (auto-transcript): “We know very well that if we serve a person who is 100% pure So we will get 100% result. So it's best. But how will we get there?”

At the kanistha stage we mostly make offences. A beginner asks to wash the guru's clothes, passes them to someone else and comes back smiling; the guru smiles too. Like meat with no bone to crack, the guru will not make it hard, and the disciple thinks he has succeeded.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:08 (auto-transcript): “Only to make offenses. It's not service. Because we don't know how to do service. You will go there and make offences only. Because, on that level, one is considered, say, Kanishtha, Kanishtha Bhakta. Because this is a star where we don't see other people, this is a star of…”

Small service leads to big service. See everyone around as the guru's own people; if not, offences undo even the little we are doing.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:08 (auto-transcript): “They say charity begins at home. Do service. Small service. We lead us to big service. So, we should consider everyone as Guru's paths as possible. Then you are on the way. If you don't see that, you are going to make offenses to contract even the little thing you are doing.”

children.topic: The pure devotee's mercy is unlimited
children.note:
Maharaj quotes the Bhagavatam's line that service to the mahat, the pure devotee of Krishna, is the doorway to liberation — the express route, as Prabhupada taught.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:58 (auto-transcript): “There is also a lot of wisdom there. Mahat jivam dharu nahu vivukti. Express route to liberation is a service to Mahat. Mahant, pure demotivate Krishna. This Shri Prabhupada taught me that he can serve the power of the good and the good and the good and the good and the good…”

children.topic: How do I know I have mercy?
children.note:
Pointing to Gita chapter 13 and serving the spiritual master, Maharaj explains: with a pure devotee's mercy, following the principles becomes easy; the mercy breaks our karma.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:13 (auto-transcript): “How do I know I have the mercy? I have the mercy of the Lord. How do I know? The same place in cottage before. Bhagavad Gita, Srimad Bhagavad Gita, Adhyaat 13. Achaara Upasana. Wishing to a special master. Prabhupada said, when one has gotten the mercy of a beauty”

One who has that mercy drops every other concern; speculation and impersonal Brahman become useless and Krishna alone matters. Mercy is not position or fame.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:23 (auto-transcript): “Everyone has the mercy of a pure devotee. One will abandon every and half only one consideration in life, the Krishna. Speculative knowledge becomes useless. Brahman becomes useless. Only Krishna becomes our primary concern. That is a mercy. Not a position.”

When Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu embraced Kesava Kasmiri, as Vrindavan Dasa Thakura describes, his pride was broken and never came back.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:20 (auto-transcript): “That is what Shri Chaitanya Maha Prabhu Keshav Kashmiri When he embraced him Vrindavan Das Thakur said He broke Keshav Kashmiri and through its sense it will never come back. He is eternally free through Godhead”

Two questions: what to do when we fail to hear, and why those closest to pure devotees sometimes fall.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:12 (auto-transcript): “What's the question? I was thinking, Gardeva, how... They are saying that the essence of Shri Prabhupada says how the essence of Sadhu Sangha is to hear. Yes. So, and then you also said that we don't hear. Yes. So then what to do then? Is it true or not? Is it true? It's…”

children.topic: Q1 · We don't hear — what then?
children.note:
Prabhupada says the essence of sadhu-sanga is hearing, yet Maharaj has said we do not hear. What should we do?

🎙 Maharaj at 49:17 (auto-transcript): “I was thinking, Gardeva, how... They are saying that the essence of Shri Prabhupada says how the essence of Sadhu Sangha is to hear. Yes. So, and then you also said that we don't hear. Yes. So then what to do then? Is it true or not? Is it true? It's true. It's true. It's…”

Continue following the instruction: sit in class and try to listen. That effort is austerity and sacrifice, it purifies, and the more we attend the more we add to our fortune. — “To sit here and try to hear it is a sacrifice.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:20 (auto-transcript): “We should continue to follow the instruction. Because it's to hear. So we should follow that principle. Sit in the speaking class. And try to listen. That's austerity. you get us purified to hear so we should continue but this thing has to hear then we will”

children.topic: Q2 · Why do close servants fall?
children.note:
Pure devotees are like fire — not too close, not too far. Many who served a pure devotee closely went down spiritually. What should we be careful about?

🎙 Maharaj at 52:34 (auto-transcript): “Thank you. Gurudev, we hear that pure devotees are like fire. And we should not go too close. and we should not be too far and we should be maintaining a good, you know, distance and relation. Plus, when we see our history, I've seen many that who are serving a pure devotee…”

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · Words Expose the Dirt Your Heart is Hiding
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Beginning SB 11.3.24 on the qualities a disciple develops to serve the guru, Maharaj dwells on cleanliness: external hygiene keeps us conscious of our purpose, but real cleanliness is of the heart, and our words and reactions show how clean or dirty it is. He ties cleanliness to goodness and the morning program, and in the questions explains how to live peacefully with those of lower standards and how to plan life so that early rising becomes natural. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The new verse lists the qualities a disciple cultivates in order to serve the spiritual master, beginning with cleanliness and austerity. It is recited, read in Hindi and English, and the purport begins with sauca, cleanliness.

The word cleanliness is not simple. Externally it means bathing, keeping even the ears clean, and having two sets of clothes so one can be washed while the other is worn.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:51 (auto-transcript): “So the word cleanliness is deep, not very simple, externally, beating three times a day, keeping our ears cleaned one who has two pairs of dress to wash at the time is dirty once”

In Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu's time a cloth once taken off was never put back on unwashed; a fresh one was worn. That was the standard he and his followers kept.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:43 (auto-transcript): “during Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's time When he removed the dress, never put it back in, it's a fresh one. It was a standard of cleanliness. That Sri Chaitanya Mahabrabhu and his followers were following. So that cleanliness was there. That is external, including our environment,…”

External cleanliness includes our environment and utensils, but the inside matters more: freedom from false pride and egotism goes deeper.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:20 (auto-transcript): “That is external, including our environment, our environment should be clean, utensils are clean, then the inside, the inside is more. It is said here in the book, one is considered internally pure when he is free from the pollution of”

Krishna instructs Uddhava on cleanliness in the varnasrama system. Maharaj quizzes the class on how many times to wash the left and right hands, and on washing after touching the mouth or the lower body.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:52 (auto-transcript): “In guiding Uddhava on the principles of Varnashram, Lord Krishna says, My dear Uddhava, general cleanliness washing the hands according to deity worship how many times how many times to wash the hand right and left yes”

Is it too much? No — such rules make us conscious of why we are here, which we usually forget. — “it's better to be conscious”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:40 (auto-transcript): “is it too much it makes one conscious of what we are here for we usually forget it's better to be conscious so this cleanness So, washing the hands, beating, and avoiding that which is untouchable.”

Both outer and inner cleanliness should come naturally to one surrendered to Krishna, not under pressure. Cleanliness prepares us for surrender, protects from Kali's influence and brings prosperity.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:48 (auto-transcript): “we should do this spontaneously not by force like the other three principles of religion cleanliness is a prerequisite for surrendering to Krishna cleanliness is for to surrender to Krishna and also I want to want”

Does bathing every day bring money while you sit at home? Maharaj laughs it off: prosperity means Krishna, and if the heart is not clean Krishna will not sit there. — “Krishna will not sit there”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:45 (auto-transcript): “if you are clean become prosperous if you are clean become rich is that getting money if you don't do anything just sit down and bet every day you get money what is prosperity we are looking at Krishna if the heart is not clean Krishna will not sit there So cleaning includes…”

Cleaning includes removing all the anarthas in the heart — not only bathing; we chant so that the heart is purified.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:27 (auto-transcript): “So cleaning includes removing all the anarthas in the heart. Not only the beating and chanting her question. We are chanting to get the hell purified. In addition, Krishna says that it is one of the 19th requisite component of knowledge. Cleanness is knowledge.”

On the purport's emphasis on inner cleansing of attachment to sense indulgence, Maharaj calls this a surgical operation: inner cleanliness shrinks as such attachment grows.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:27 (auto-transcript): “excessive attachment we're dealing with internally this is This is a surgical operation, cleansing excessive attachment to indulgence in sex life. Cleanness is curtailed in proportion to one's growing attachment for women or men.”

What we speak shows how clean or dirty our heart is. As we chant, our words should become clean too — no abusive or needless talk.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:01 (auto-transcript): “that is what we speak it will reflect how clean or dirty the heart is the heart should be clean as we are chanting our words by avoiding abusive and unnecessary talk this is cleanness Our words should be pure should be clean clean words which means avoiding abusive words”

Be careful with the words we use: the way we speak and the way we respond to situations display the heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:29 (auto-transcript): “Our words should be pure should be clean clean words which means avoiding abusive words which means to mind our words to be careful with the kind of words we use because it means the heart is dead the way we use words the way we respond to situations yesterday”

children.topic: 'How are you able to do this?'
children.note:
A devotee asked Maharaj yesterday, and another has asked many times, what lets him act as he does. He did not answer then; the answer is here — it comes from the heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:11 (auto-transcript): “yesterday a devotee asked me how did you how are you able to do this I didn't answer. I hope the devotees get the answer from here. And teacher Prabhu also asked me many times. How do you do? What motivates you to do like this? What?”

If there is no anger inside, no one can provoke it; the same with lust, envy and anxiety. The strength of everything we do comes from the nature of the heart. — “no one can make you angry”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:18 (auto-transcript): “The heart tells everything inside. If everything is inside, it will show outside. if you don't have anger inside no one can make you angry if you don't have loss inside nobody can make you lost there is no envy inside situation cannot make you envious nobody can put you in…”

children.topic: How does the steady one speak?
children.note:
Arjuna asked Krishna how one fixed in wisdom speaks and behaves. If he reacted the way we do, what would be the difference? The difference must be clear: our speech shows the state of our heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:29 (auto-transcript): “I said, Arjuna asked Krishna. A sthita pragya. What is his life? How can I know? Krishna said to give answer. Arjuna asked. Does he respond to the situation the way I am doing? Krishna said, no. if he responds the same day what's the difference the difference is very clear so…”

This is the value of sastra-caksu: when we see or hear someone, we check with scripture to understand who this person is, and then we know how to live with them.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:40 (auto-transcript): “So, can you see the importance of Sastra Chakshu? When you see someone doing something when you hear someone saying something their minds come to the scripture to check who is this person and then you would know how to live with that person with that difficulty right a…”

children.topic: A brahmana with an unclean neighbour
children.note:
How can a very clean brahmana live peacefully with someone of lower habits? By tolerance: he keeps himself clean and understands the other's nature instead of fighting.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:17 (auto-transcript): “a brahmana who is very clean how do you stay comfortable with a dirty person How can they live with anyone else? Right? The Brahman, very clean, and the Sudra, of course, the Sudra quality is very high. So less than Sudra, yes, less than Sudra. The Sudra's lakshan is very…”

We struggle in relationships because we only present our own case and forget the other's. Without brahminical qualities, negative moods take over. — “we refuse to understand other person”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:04 (auto-transcript): “you see why we have difficulty in relationship we have difficulty in relationship because of selfishness we refuse to understand other person their relationship will be difficult I only present my case I am forgetting your case So no Brahmanic quality, then the mood will…”

children.topic: Set the standard and say it
children.note:
Keeping Krishna in the centre needs proper communication: set the standard and make sure it is communicated; otherwise passion and ignorance pull you in.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:19 (auto-transcript): “Proper communication. How do you do that? Yes. Say the standard. Make sure you communicate it. Right? It's not a standard and you communicate it. Otherwise, the passionate mood will put you in. Ignorance will bring you in. You have to maintain. That's the quality of the…”

Two devotees came to Maharaj shouting at each other. He only looked at them and stayed quiet; after a few minutes they left in shame and solved it themselves. They wanted to draw him into their mood, and he refused.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:00 (auto-transcript): “one day two devotees they were shouting at each other and they came to me they were shouting at each other so I looked at them and came quiet after a few minutes they left for the shame they wanted to put me in their mood and I refused they solved themselves their problem…”

Srila Prabhupada taught that a Krishna conscious person is always clean, asked that the temple be kept spotless and that hands be washed before touching anything of Krishna's, because Krishna is the purest. It was on his mind even in his last days.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:24 (auto-transcript): “clean next is godliness So the Prabhupada instructed and taught us in that way Another thing I request is that everything in the temple should be kept nice and clean Everyone should wash hands before touching anything of Krishna's We should always remember that Krishna is the…”

Goodness means clean. Rising early, bathing, tilaka, the holy name, mangala-arati, tulasi and guru-puja, Bhagavatam and prasada — all are in goodness. That is the platform Prabhupada raised us to; we start from here.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:41 (auto-transcript): “which is satwagun means what? It's clean. It's clean. So, you see what is happening? What is happening is the process of cleaning the heart. The environment for cleaning. The things used for cleaning. All are in goodness. That is the platform Shlava Prabhupada raised all of…”

Suta Gosvami says Krishna came for those in goodness. Someone worried about his stomach thinks God means daily bread; a brahmana thinks of Krishna. So cleaning the heart is very important.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:03 (auto-transcript): “So, Sutta Goswami first kandha Bhagavatam he said Lord Krishna came for those who are in the mood of goodness. Why goodness? Because that is the foundation to Anasana Krishna. Someone who is worried about his stomach. What will Anasana about God? God for him means what?”

Two questions: living alongside those of lower standards, and how to make early rising a lifelong habit.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:20 (auto-transcript): “Any comments? Questions? Comment? Hare Krishna, Gurudev. Thank you for the lecture. My question was that you were mentioning how to live like a Brahmana living with a less than Shudra. So in matter of cleanliness also plus in matter of speech, the dealings also. So can we…”

How does one with a brahmana's standard live alongside someone far below it, in cleanliness, speech and dealings?

🎙 Maharaj at 49:26 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Gurudev. Thank you for the lecture. My question was that you were mentioning how to live like a Brahmana living with a less than Shudra. So in matter of cleanliness also plus in matter of speech, the dealings also. So can we elaborate more about this? So,…”

As Prabhupada said, always neat and clean: set the standard and keep reminding everyone of the importance of cleanliness inside and out. — “The standard should be set.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:31 (auto-transcript): “The standard has to be set. As Prabhupada is saying, Always neat and clean. Always neat and clean. The standard should be set. And then you have to continuously remind us. The importance of clearly Both inside and outside Inside We should hear the scripture To change the holy…”

children.topic: Clean the heart in the dhama
children.note:
Inside, we clean the heart by hearing scripture, chanting, hearing Krishna's pastimes and thinking of devotees and the holy dhama. While physically here, visit the pastime places and join kirtan with the heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:08 (auto-transcript): “Inside We should hear the scripture To change the holy name Hear the persons of Krishna Think about devotees Think about the holy dham All these are for cleaning the heart. Take full advantage. Especially when we are physically here. Visit past time bliss of Krishna. And do…”

Yesterday we heard Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's benediction for singing the Gurvastaka with care: one attains Krishna. We sing it daily, yet many heard its meaning for the first time — that is laziness, not assessing what is available.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:06 (auto-transcript): “Yesterday We got We listened to the benediction Benediction From Vishnu Chakravati Thakur and we are going to chant it for our entire life. There are eight of them. And the ninety-one is a benediction for the person who composed it. Do you remember?”

In Lagos, Nigeria, before chanting a prayer the benediction is explained first, so devotees put their minds into it. Once they understood, their enthusiasm was different; they even asked to continue rather than finish.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:44 (auto-transcript): “In Lagos, Nigeria. In Lagos, Nigeria. Before we turn some mantras, I will go to the benediction first. So that we can put our mind there. So you know what you're going to get from this. Then when you start doing it, you put your mind into it because you know what to get. That…”

A brahmana's mercy is to perform austerity to raise others' standards without fighting. That is the strength of his practice — it is a prayer.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:27 (auto-transcript): “The Brahman is merciful. What is the mercifulness? He has to do austerity to raise other standards without fighting. That is the strength of his practice. It's a prayer. It's a prayer. All right. Hare Krishna. Yes. Hare Krishna, are you there? Yesterday you gave one statement…”

children.topic: Q2 · How to rise early, every day?
children.note:
Finishing sixteen rounds before mangala-arati is hard. Practically, how should one sleep, eat and live to rise early consistently, when life is busy and unplanned?

🎙 Maharaj at 58:06 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, are you there? Yesterday you gave one statement that one who is not chanting or completing his first 16 rounds before Mangala Arthi, he's lazy. So, to do this is very difficult. So, we are constantly hearing that we have to arise very early in the morning and do…”

children.topic: The ashram is organised; we aren't
children.note:
An ashram is planned and spiritual; we make it material, and complications follow. — “It is we who are not planned.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:15 (auto-transcript): “It is we who are not planned. What is the Ashram? Ashram is planned. organized, well organized we are not organized not the ashram it is called ashram it is spiritual we make it material then complications come there yesterday we discussed that you know that you are attending…”

Late programs, then ten chapatis, five sabjis, litres of water, milk and gulab jamun before sleep — did the ashram design that? Then the body is tired and will not rise or concentrate, even if forced.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:46 (auto-transcript): “yesterday we discussed that you know that you are attending a program is late and then 10 o'clock 11 o'clock you are eating 10 chapati 5 sabjis 2 liters of water Then you drink milk And go to sleep Then gulab jamun Is the ashram that designed that”

As Prabhupada said, devotees should mould their lives to stay Krishna conscious twenty-four hours. Non-devotees are very organised for sense gratification and accept austerities without grudge.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:13 (auto-transcript): “we should plan it As the prophet said, we, devotees, to mold our lives in such a way that we remain 24 hours Krishna conscious. Planning. We have to plan it. the people we call non-devotees they are very organized for their sanctification they are very organized”

Bilvamangala Thakura used a corpse as a boat to cross the river and a snake as a rope to climb the wall for his pleasure. No one forced him; he saw only the enjoyment waiting. If we look at Krishna, austerity becomes a joy.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:12 (auto-transcript): “just a scripturally example there are so many material examples just take a look at this scriptural example a sastry udharan Bilmangal Thakur Indri Bhog he used a snake to climb the fence Was your austerity for him or is it a pleasure? See? What for us? Oh, Prabhupada didn't…”

A student stays up all night with coffee and his feet in water to pass an exam, and no teacher told him to; he designed it to reach his goal. We did not complain then — now we complain. That is laziness.

maps.title: Become the Disciple · Day 09 · When the Mind Says NO, Tapasya Says CONTINUE

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · When the Mind Says NO, Tapasya Says CONTINUE
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up tapah, austerity: staying fixed in one's duty while the mind pushes back, because lust, the eternal enemy, can only be conquered this way. He presents Ekadasi as the first meaning of austerity, a caring mother that shapes and polishes our lives, and answers questions on fasting beyond the body's limits and on breaking vows. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse lists the qualities a disciple learns while serving the spiritual master; yesterday covered the first, today the second. Maharaj says these qualities are not decoration but the training itself.

To be a doctor you go to medical college; to be a pilot you learn navigation at an aeronautical college. To be a good disciple we are told to develop these qualities, or we will not succeed — like a student who never gets the answer right. — “So these qualities are necessary.”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:10 (auto-transcript): “to be a doctor this qualification he must go to medical college to be a pilot he must go to aeronautical college and learn all the details about navigation and to be a good disciple”

The qualities grow by themselves as we practise, but if we deliberately work on them we move faster. That is why the Yogendras taught them to Maharaja Nimi.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:47 (auto-transcript): “they will develop as we keep practicing still, if we consciously work on these qualities It will be better. We will move faster. Therefore, they are necessary. That is why the Yujandras taught them to Maharaj Nimi and for Rosh to follow.”

Austerity means holding to one's duty while the mind throws up irrational impulses. Maharaj asks the room twice whether they understand this phrase.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:45 (auto-transcript): “So the next item is Tapaha. Tapaha or austerity means that despite the irrational impulses of the mind, one should remain fixed in executing his proper duty in life. You understand?”

children.topic: Demands last as long as the body
children.note:
While we have a body its demands for gratification continue; to transcend the body, austerity is the most important tool. Look at the Vedas and the sages — austerity is everywhere prominent.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:48 (auto-transcript): “as long as you have this body the demands for gratification will continue we transcend them we transcend the body to transcend the body austerity is most important”
Citing Bhagavad-gita 5.23, Maharaj calls this the assignment of a whole lifetime: before this body ends, the impulses must be conquered.

Rupa Gosvami's instruction is recalled: one whose senses are fully under control — held in the palm of the hand — is qualified to be a guru for the whole world.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:28 (auto-transcript): “Prabhupada Goswami mentioned this same thing The qualification for someone to become Jagat Guru is what, all the senses are under their control. In their palm. Right? It must be in our palm. Yes, especially one most controlled burning anger and the urge for one-toned sex life.”

children.topic: Human life is for Krishna consciousness
children.note:
Animals have no religion and no scripture; only humans do. So neglecting Krishna consciousness is itself a violation of human life and a very big offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:29 (auto-transcript): “So if one is not a devotee, That is, that itself is a violation of human life. It's a very big offense. Not to take to Krishna consciousness. because human form of life is meant for this so we don't see animals having religion animals don't have scripture”

children.topic: Not taking to it is offence
children.note:
Maharaj says plainly that a human being who does not practise Krishna consciousness is automatically an offender, because the human form exists for this. — “Not to take to Krishna consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:52 (auto-transcript): “It's a very big offense. Not to take to Krishna consciousness. because human form of life is meant for this so we don't see animals having religion animals don't have scripture only human beings have scripture so if you don't practice Krishna consciously We are offenders.”

We owe Krishna, the sages, the demigods, our parents, society and the king. Krishna consciousness is the one payment that clears every debt; otherwise we live a condemned life. — “The only way to pay is to take to Krishna consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:37 (auto-transcript): “Automatically, we are offenders. To Krishna. To the sages. To demigods. Parents. Society. The king, we are, we are debtors to all of them. The only way to pay is to take to Krishna consciousness.”

Lust, anger and greed overpower almost everyone, but devotees have the process, the knowledge and the support to conquer them. Without control we cannot be selfless, and without selflessness we cannot be good servants.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:40 (auto-transcript): “Only devotees Only devotees We have the process We have the knowledge we have the support so we can do it so this is our concern we cannot help purely if we are not selfless we cannot be a good servant”

Through Bhagavad-gita 18.45 and Bhaktivinoda Thakura, the purport teaches that one need not become a monk or a forest yogi; offering one's work to Krishna and taking shelter of the holy name brings perfection within ordinary daily life.

Maharaj recalls a great devotee's words that going off to the Himalayas to practise alone is selfish and lacks compassion. Bhaktivinoda Thakura's advice is to stay where we are and chant nicely among devotees, guided by our spiritual master.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:14 (auto-transcript): “Lord Maharaj said, going to the forest to practice with spiritual Himalayas selfishness. They are not compassionate. so Bhaktivinathakura said remain in our position and turn Hare Krishna nicely in association of devotees guided by one of our spiritual master”

Silence is one of the qualities in the verse, but our understanding of it is different from sitting quietly in a cave; it is best practised in Krishna consciousness. — “mechanical silence is useless”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:17 (auto-transcript): “so called silence silence is mentioned here as one of the qualities but our understanding of our silence is different mechanical silence is useless it is best practice in Krishna consciousness Unfortunately, if a human being neglects the regulative principles of civilized life”

Maharaj asks how many of Caitanya Mahaprabhu's followers were sannyasis. Only a handful; all the rest were householders, fully engaged and chanting, and all were successful. Our system has a perfect arrangement for everyone — we simply follow sincerely. — “It is a tested and approved method for success.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:31 (auto-transcript): “How many of his devotees are Sanyasi? Many. Disciples How many are Sanyases? Six Goswami, that is one Then They came after Before them Savadhamadha Goswami Keshava Keshava Keshava Barati Keshava Barati Paramananda Puri Paramananda Parati also”
Bhagavad-gita 3.39 calls lust the eternal enemy that covers knowledge and burns like fire. Austerity means not becoming impatient or unregulated under its waves, and those of anger and greed.

Maharaj quizzes the class. Answers come: it can never be satisfied; it is one of the three gates to hell. But anger and greed are gates too, and are not called eternal enemies — lust is singled out because it is their source.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:38 (auto-transcript): “Why loss is eternal enemy? It's our word. Do you understand it? Eternal enemy. Why is it eternal enemy? It cannot be satisfied. It cannot be satisfied. The which is Nitya Vahidana. What else? Why loss is Nitya Vahidana? One of the gates to hell. But other three are not said…”

Intelligent generals study the opponent's strength before battle; most of us want to fight without knowing what we face. On the battlefield of Kurukshetra Duryodhana pointed out to his teacher how cleverly the other side had arranged its forces.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:34 (auto-transcript): “Intelligent persons before the fight. they will check the strength of the enemy is it not they will before you fight they will spy what is the strength of the enemy most of us want to fight they don't know the strength of the enemy how do you succeed I will succeed you cannot…”

Lust is pure love of God transformed, as milk becomes yogurt: it comes from milk but can no longer act as milk. Because our love for Krishna is eternal, its perverted form is an eternal enemy while we are conditioned.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:28 (auto-transcript): “So she gave the answer. Lost is the opposite of pure love of Godhead. Pure love of Godhead is changed. Like when milk is transformed into yogurt, right? Can you remove yogurt from milk? No, it is coming from milk, but it cannot act as milk any longer because of transformation.”

Maharaj recalls the business term he was searching for: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats. Intelligence is given to study the enemy carefully and then plan. — “we should know, then we can plan.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:04 (auto-transcript): “I remember the word I was looking for SWOT analysis SWOT analysis SWOT analysis SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT The strength, weakness, opportunity, threats, threats, threats, we should know, then we can plan.”

Having studied the enemy, the remedy is clear: austerity is not optional. Without it we cannot control ourselves or succeed.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:22 (auto-transcript): “then what's the remedy austerity is compulsory compulsory not not optional if you want to control So, austerity, austerity, without austerity, we cannot make it compulsory. So, we are looking at this, we are looking at this, we need austerity to become successful.”

Srila Prabhupada translates tapah first as fasting on certain days of the month. So when we hear the word austerity, Maharaj says, the first thing that should come to mind is Ekadasi.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:18 (auto-transcript): “So when we hear austerity, what are we talking about? What is the first thing to come to the mind? What is the first thing to come to the mind? When we hear tapah, immediately you should remember Ekadasi. They say tapahshyabhundain, that's the first one.”

Who cares for us? Ekadasi cares — she keeps us on track, fixes and polishes our lives and makes them offerable, as gold is valued only after passing through fire. — “Ekadashi shapes our lives”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:14 (auto-transcript): “Wow. Mother. Our mother. Who cares? Who cares? Ekadashi cares Mood our life Keep us on track Ekadashi shapes our lives He fixes it properly Fix our life Ekadashi polish our lives and make it offerable make it like gold gold is not appreciated”

Austerity is uncomfortable for body and mind but favourable for spiritual realisation. After an Ekadasi fast you feel happy the next day that you did it; what is very comfortable for mind and body is not where an intelligent person goes.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:44 (auto-transcript): “not comfortable for the body not shooting the mind but conducive to a spiritual realization that's austerity that is Ekadashi that shapes our lives Ekadashi gives purpose to our life in Christianity polish it”

Austerity is not for mystic power or material gain. By reducing the body's demands we clear the cloud between us and Krishna; we were expanded for his enjoyment, and by not giving it we pay heavily. — “The goal of austerity is to please Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:10 (auto-transcript): “Confirmed in the Bhagavatam. The goal of austerity is to please Krishna. Yes, that is the goal. I want to please Krishna.”

Animals do not work for their sense gratification, yet they get it free and without tension; we pay heavily and live in anxiety. So Krishna gives regulative principles for freedom — Ekadasi frees us and should be welcomed happily, not treated as just another day.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:41 (auto-transcript): “that we can get in the material world if you look very carefully Animals, do they work for their sanctification like human beings? Animals, do they work for their sanctification like human beings? They are getting or not? They are getting. Free.”

Maharaj stresses this is not his own recommendation: in Puri, Caitanya Mahaprabhu told the devotees not even to remember food on Ekadasi, keeping even Jagannatha's mahaprasada for the next day, and to spend the day only chanting and hearing the Bhagavatam. The devotees were happy and some went on parikrama.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:24 (auto-transcript): “This is not my recommendation. This is Chaitanya Mahabharata's recommendation. Jagannath Puri to Jagannath Pundit. Put in his book. Premi Barata. Yes, very sweet. Sweet necklace. Clearly written. It's clearly written. Chaitanya Mahabharata said. Today is a kadashi. Therefore,…”

Fasting on Ekadasi and Janmastami and keeping vows such as a householder's celibacy are devotional austerities; devotees who keep them faithfully are rarely in want. — “If you practice this nicely, you will never lack anything, materially, spiritually.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:37 (auto-transcript): “Because devotees are faithful to these practices. They rarely find themselves in a condition of want. If you practice this nicely, you will never lack anything, materially, spiritually.”

Two questions on austerity and the body, ahead of the Kartika vows.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:33 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Hare Krishna. and I feel that I can do a lot of kastriyaki. So, can I just depend on Krishna for my bodily help? Because we hear from different speakers that Krishna only protects your subtle body, not the physical body. Mataji's question is that I want to do a lot of…”

children.topic: Q1 · Fast hard and trust Krishna?
children.note:
A Mataji wants to do a lot of austerity and asks whether she can depend on Krishna for her body, since some speakers say he protects only the subtle body.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:47 (auto-transcript): “and I feel that I can do a lot of kastriyaki. So, can I just depend on Krishna for my bodily help? Because we hear from different speakers that Krishna only protects your subtle body, not the physical body. Mataji's question is that I want to do a lot of kastriyaki, and I…”

Krishna protects his devotee completely. One who practises sincerely and lives a steady life finds the material and spiritual sides balanced.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:15 (auto-transcript): “Krishna protects his devotee completely. Not so, completely. Mission and devotee sincerely practice this and really have any want.”

children.topic: Do what the body can handle
children.note:
If the body does not adjust to the austerity you want, reduce it to what it can bear. — “So we don't do things we cannot handle.”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:33 (auto-transcript): “So if the body is not adjusting to a structure as you want, so reduce it to what the body can handle. So we don't do things we cannot handle.”

children.topic: Better to leave the body fasting
children.note:
When the mind is purified one thinks: let Krishna's will be done, but this is what I will do for him — and goes ahead without missing anything. Maharaj recalls Haridasa Thakura at his departure, who could neither refuse prasadam nor take it fully, and so honoured it while continuing his fast.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:24 (auto-transcript): “When the mind has become purified to a certain stage. One would think. What Krishna wants, let it be. But this is what I want to do for Krishna. Go ahead to do it. You will not miss anything. It's better if I want to fast while living the body than to eat till they're living…”

The mind discourages us, as the gopis' parents doubted they could manage. Knowing they wanted Krishna as their husband, the gopis bathed in the cold Yamuna every winter dawn and ate saltless, spiceless khichri for a month — and on the very last day Krishna appeared.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:09 (auto-transcript): “Since our mind is not strong They want to do something Their mind will start to discourage us The gopis Were told by their parents we have never seen you do this kind of austerity before so how will you be able to do this you can't do it”

children.topic: Q2 · What if I break my vow?
children.note:
Every Kartika Maharaj is asked this before the vow has even begun. Planning for failure is very dangerous; a slip by miscalculation, followed by serious repentance, is different from searching for a loophole — Krishna cannot be cheated, only ourselves. — “we can only do that to ourselves”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:22 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, what a person who did not complete his vow. We have not started. We are already prepared for not completing. Every year I get this. I'm sure next year we'll get the same question. Very good. No, this year. I'll get the question. Means what? We are preparing to break.”

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · A Devotee's Victory is Tolerance, Not Revenge
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains titiksa, tolerance: the forgiving nature without which a devotee cannot preach, chant without offence or find peace. Through the tree, the cat and the dog, a slap returned, and a man who forgave a broken windscreen, he shows that tolerance spares us suffering, and in the questions he separates personal forbearance from a leader's duty to correct wrongdoing. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Today's quality from the verse is tolerance. The purport explains that a world full of irritations will infect a devotee with a spirit of revenge unless he is very forgiving.

Tolerance is praised throughout the Gita, the Bhagavatam and the Mahabharata as a quality of a sadhu. Srila Prabhupada gives two examples of it: Lord Jesus Christ and Haridasa Thakura.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:16 (auto-transcript): “Pahen Shil Describe in many places Bhagavad Gita Two Bhagavatam also Shri Mahabhatam All the qualities of a sadhu This is a tradition And the Pope and Prabhupada give an example of Lord Jesus Christ.”

Haridasa Thakura was beaten, Jesus was crucified and Nityananda Prabhu was wounded — all because they were preaching. Maharaj repeats the point in Hindi for everyone. — “One is not tolerant, one cannot preach.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:16 (auto-transcript): “Haridash Thakur was tortured because he was preaching. This way he was crucified because he was preaching. Isai Masih ko maar diya gaya kiyo? Kiyo ki whe prachar kar raha thay. Bhagwaan Yityananda Prabhu ko bhot ghayal kar diya gaya kiyo? Whe prachar kar raha thay. One is not…”

Bhismadeva taught Maharaja Yudhisthira that forgiveness is how anger is controlled. All these qualities, Maharaj notes, are connected to one another.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:58 (auto-transcript): “One was thought is forgiving. Forgiveness, forgiveness. Which is also one of the ways to control anger. Shri Bishmadev was teaching Yudhisthira Maharaj. Shri Bishmadev was teaching Maharaj Yudhisthira to control anger, one must practice forgiveness. All these qualities, they…”

For a brahmana tolerance comes with preaching; for a kshatriya it comes with managing a movement, tolerating some disobedience and also punishing when necessary. But every devotee needs it for chanting without offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:48 (auto-transcript): “So for Brahmana, tolerance comes from preaching. For Shatriyas, the challenges of managing a preaching movement, management, if you want to be successful, tolerance is required. I have to tolerate some disobedient citizens.”

Offenceless chanting requires tolerating the senses and the mind. Maharaj warns that one who chants nicely meets more problems than others, as a reaction to that potent chanting. — “you will have more problem than others”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:13 (auto-transcript): “requires tolerance we have to treat dictated senses especially if you are chanting nicely you will have more problem than others because Because the reaction from your potent chanting.”
Referring to Bhagavad-gita 2.70, Maharaj says that whoever runs wherever the senses push can never be peaceful. To be peaceful, do not respond; keep quiet and engage more in the process.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu's example: the tree stands through wind, rain, sun and snow and remains peaceful. A devotee should be more tolerant than a tree.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:01 (auto-transcript): “For example, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu gives Chaitanya Mahaprabhu The example Chaitanya Mahaprabhu gives is the nature of the tree Chaitanya Mahaprabhu leaves branches and it leaves leaves leaves”

A tree gives fruit, shade, medicine and oxygen free, without discrimination — whoever comes may take. It is not standing for itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:38 (auto-transcript): “a tree gives fruit gives shade gives medicine oxygen completely free no discrimination only you can take me whoever comes take So the tree is standing not for itself.”

We mistreat the tree and it does not protest; cut down, it gives firewood for sacrifice, cooking and heating a home, and even its ashes and charcoal are useful, charcoal being part of a blood tonic. — “The tree will not stop giving service.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:33 (auto-transcript): “Yet, we mistreated the tree. We put the tree with it. We put the tree with it. The tree will not protest. And even the tree is cut down. The tree will not stop giving service. who will continue to give service they cut down the tree they will not give you fruit but they will…”

children.topic: When to tolerate, when to act
children.note:
Mahaprabhu, who gave the tree example, also showed when tolerance applies: when his devotees were attacked, as with Nityananda Prabhu and Haridasa Thakura, he was ready to act against the offenders.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:48 (auto-transcript): “Chitanya Mahaprabhu Chitanya Mahaprabhu Vrachshaki tulna says that He taught us when to apply tolerance and win. that when there is a seal and there is no seal.”

Maharaj's simple rule: if you will not tolerate, you simply suffer; if you do not want to suffer, tolerate. Answering in kind brings the suffering home.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:11 (auto-transcript): “I will mention before tolerance if you don't want to tolerate you simply suffer if you don't want to suffer tolerate if you don't want to suffer tolerate if you want to suffer don't tolerate whatever happens”

children.topic: Slap back, end up in jail
children.note:
Someone slaps you and you slap back; he falls dead. You are not promoted to general — you are a murderer. He slapped first, but he did not kill you; now you go to jail.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:57 (auto-transcript): “Someone slap you, slap the patient back. The patient falls on dead. You get the promotion. The promotion will give you big rank. General. No, you'll be cute. They said, no, no, but he slapped me first. He slapped me to teach him a hand that I am not so cheap like that. So I…”

Or you fight back, both get wounded, and at the hospital you explain you were teaching him a lesson out of mercy, so please treat me free. The hospital agrees you are very compassionate — and hands you the bill. — “your compassion is going to pay me $10,000”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:14 (auto-transcript): “if you slap the person back he will keep quiet he will be and you had that and then wounds hospital you tell the doctor somebody slapped me and I slapped the person back because if I don't do that to the person today tomorrow we'll do the same thing to stop the person”

Krishna used the Pandavas to show us the level of tolerance through all their difficulties, and that tolerance gave them a power to control Krishna himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:12 (auto-transcript): “Tolerance is the quality of it, I have to think the ability, Panamanji, he was discussing with Naradamuni, He said, the Pandavas, Krishna used them to teach us the level of their tolerance, all the difficulties they passed through.”

Krishna, their messenger and Arjuna's chariot driver, wanted to return to Dvaraka; asked to stay one more week, he stayed. He left the sages meditating on him in the forest for years and forgot his own city to live with Yudhisthira. — “That is the level of Pandavas.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:29 (auto-transcript): “The Pandavas met Krishna, their messenger, see not, they met Krishna, their saraband, driving Arjuna's child who was 18 days, they detained Krishna, the mother was detained Krishna the Krishna wanted to go to Dwaraka you just said Maharaj can you stay for one more week what…”

Because people today cannot control mind and senses or tell body from soul, they become intolerant at small inconveniences. If we want real convenience, Maharaj says, we must first control the senses.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:36 (auto-transcript): “The inability of people in this age to control their mind and senses. To understand the workings of nature's laws. and to know the difference between body and soul means that they become intolerant at the slightest inconvenience we become intolerant of our senses”

A cat sees something, closes its eyes and stays peaceful; a dog sees the same thing and barks and runs about in anxiety. Tolerance brings peace.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:12 (auto-transcript): “a cat cats see something to close his eyes remain peaceful a dog see the same thing is that peaceful Patting means what? Restless, anxiety, tension. But the cat is peaceful. Peaceful. He saw it. He closes his eyes.”

Devotees learn these qualities from scripture, take them in and finally realise them, while life itself supplies plenty of practice. Prahlada Maharaja tolerated his father, and children taught tolerance early are equipped for spiritual progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:30 (auto-transcript): “Yes. For the reason, the voters need to regularly study these practices from scripture. Then I simulate and finally realize them. Meanwhile, both the execution of devotional service and residence in this material world offers plenty of opportunity to practice facing dualities…”

Tolerate the senses, the mind, the body's demands and others, who act differently according to the modes controlling them — and tolerate Krishna, waiting for his mercy without questioning; then he helps us succeed. — “we have to tolerate Lord Krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:11 (auto-transcript): “To tolerate the senses, tolerate the mind, tolerate the body's demands, tolerate others, understand that we are of different nature we are going to act differently based on the mood which is controlling us we have to tolerate Lord Krishna”

Three questions: the consciousness behind tolerance, a leader's duty to correct, and how pure devotees train their disciples.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:23 (auto-transcript): “comment, question, questions yes want to tolerate or not okay thank you No, I cannot take it anymore. It is too much of you. I've been tolerating for all these years. Today, I can't take it. It's too much. How long will I continue like this? This is nonsense. Thank you.”

children.topic: Q1 · What consciousness makes tolerance devotional?
children.note:
The Pandavas tolerated, but so do yogis in the forest. With what consciousness should a devotee forgive — by giving the benefit of the doubt, or by accepting how the person is?

🎙 Maharaj at 36:15 (auto-transcript): “When you are saying more pandas, they were tolerating. And then they did it in Krishna. So I was thinking even the UBs who were meditating in the forest of the UBs, they were also tolerating. So I think that it's not only tolerance, it's the consciousness of how you are…”

From scripture we know that what happens to us is merited; the other person is only an instrument and I am the cause of my suffering. — “This knowledge helps one to tolerate.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:19 (auto-transcript): “It means that I have the knowledge from the scripture that what is happening to me, I merit it. This person is acting as an instrument.”

Before coming to Krishna consciousness Maharaj saw a madman smash a man's windscreen. Guards were beating him, but the owner said let him go: in a past life I broke his, and now my karma has left me. Moved, Maharaj joined the same mystical order before finding the temple nearby.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:34 (auto-transcript): “I mentioned before, what took me to join one mystical organization, Roshikurshan Order. Roshikurshan Order. A madman broke his windscreen. The security guards were beating the man. But the man told him to leave him. I was watching the scene.”

children.topic: A sadhu should not add karma
children.note:
Knowing we are responsible makes us peaceful, like the cat rather than the dog. A sadhu does not increase his karma by answering people in the same way they treat him.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:11 (auto-transcript): “So when one knows, I am responsible for what is happening to me. You'll be happy. I'll be happy. Because as the Bhakti Dhanas is what Takurupa always said, a sadhu should not increase his karma. Sadhu should tolerate. Don't respond the same way when then people will treat us.…”

children.topic: Q2 · When should a leader correct?
children.note:
If a leader keeps silent and accepts everything as karma, will a culture of misbehaviour grow? How much should be accepted, and when should one act?

🎙 Maharaj at 45:02 (auto-transcript): “I was trying to understand, in continuation, the question, when this quality comes to that of the leaders, you mentioned we should know how to tolerate and then to punish. Here you brought in a point that we should always know that the way certain people are believing is…”

children.topic: Insults to you, insults to devotees
children.note:
If someone insults you, tolerate it; if he insults a devotee, correct it. Not correcting sends the message to the whole community that anyone may be insulted, while correction sends the opposite message.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:26 (auto-transcript): “Devotee, he sought another devotee. and you have seen it you correct it if the person insult you you tolerate it if he is a salt or a devotee you correct it if you don't correct it you have sent a message to the whole community that in this community”

Maharaj has seen leaders in bad health because they did not respond to wrongdoing. Correct it and Krishna protects you; neglect it and you are not representing him. That neglect is not tolerance. If it is beyond you, take it higher. — “take it to the appropriate quarters”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:01 (auto-transcript): “that will pollute that environment I've seen some of our leaders in a very bad health because they don't respond to wrongdoings when they're supposed to When you do it, they didn't correct it, it's affecting the health.”

When his devotees were attacked, Caitanya Mahaprabhu did not say, never mind, these things happen while preaching, you are not the body. He acted, and so should we. Slights to oneself because of one's position, though, can be let go.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:56 (auto-transcript): “honest means we are giving to wrongdoers we gave an example of Chaitanya Mahabhu he didn't come and tell the time oh I'm very sorry for this just forgive them they're useless he didn't do that you know these are the things expected while you are preaching you know just to…”

children.topic: Q3 · Do pure devotees correct indirectly?
children.note:
Pure devotees sometimes seem not to punish outright but to correct in other ways — even by glorifying the person in front of everyone. What is in their mind?

🎙 Maharaj at 53:01 (auto-transcript): “he fell down. So when I see the feelings of pure devotees, sometimes it's not just they would straight away give the punishment or give it outrightly, but there might be other ways. So even in a related discussion, I can understand by glorifying that devotee in front of…”

Maharaj's Gurudev gave some disciples the sannyasa cloth but told them not to wear it yet; he praised another as the best president, and that disciple simply enjoyed the praise. Each was a test, and none is promoted without passing. — “A teacher who does not give test is not a good teacher.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:36 (auto-transcript): “So, when he was glorifying his devotee, when I fluttered him, he gave him a chance. He demonstrated how you are the best president. He didn't face it properly. But he was simply enjoying the, he didn't remember that the sita is on there.”

A godbrother who was corrected and given other service asked instead to go to India to be purified; Gurudev said, take my blessings. Maharaj told him the real blessing was the first instruction. He went, stayed a year, returned to Nigeria and left the movement.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:03 (auto-transcript): “One of the God brothers. He did something wrong, and Gurudev punished him, and he gave me a different service. See, he went and told Gurudev, Gurudev, now I am contaminated, so I want to go to India, Instead of the service you give to me, I want to go to India to get…”
