nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The last quality in the verse is equanimity amid heat and cold, happiness and distress. With Bhagavad-gita 2.14–15, Srila Prabhupada's letter to a disciple in the Vrindavan summer and a tragic quarrel on a Lagos bridge, Maharaj shows that dualities are temporary, come from the mind and our own past actions, and are transcended by practising tolerance. The questions turn to knowing people's natures, the limits of tolerance for a ruler, and making time for sadhana. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The final quality in the verse: staying steady through material dualities such as heat and cold, happiness and distress. The purport points to Bhagavad-gita 2.14.

One should stay calm even when disturbing dualities appear. Tolerance was discussed earlier; this point is about facing the pairs of opposites.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:47 (auto-transcript): “One should keep a cool head even when disturbing material dualities become manifesting. We have discussed tolerance.”

Ups and downs belong to the conditioned state, so we should not be surprised by them, any more than we are surprised to be hungry. What has gone up will come down. — “I'm hungry because I have a material body.”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:48 (auto-transcript): “And we shouldn't be surprised. Just like when do you get surprised why I am hungry? I'm hungry because I have a material body. If one has a spiritual body, he will not be hungry. So one should not be surprised with us and dance. So you know, as he has gone up, he's going to…”

Krishna speaks of sita and usna, cold and heat. We are now in summer; tolerate it, because in a short while it will go and another situation will come. Happiness and distress are likewise already allotted to this body.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:48 (auto-transcript): “Shita and Osana. Shita and Osana. Thandi and Garmi. Winter and Summer. we are part of this material world now we are going through summer so we should tolerate it”

We do not invite distress, yet it comes; our past actions called it, just as they call our happiness. The wise therefore advise simply tolerating, if we want peace. — “Our actions have called for it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:38 (auto-transcript): “We don't call distress, he comes. We don't call distress. Our actions have called for it. The same thing, happiness will come. Because we have called for them. For one who wants to be peaceful in this world, Don't disturb yourself with it. Srila Prabhupada wrote a letter to…”

A disciple from a cold country arrived in India in summer and suffered like a fish out of water. Prabhupada wrote that he had accustomed his body to cold and now in Vrindavan could adjust it to heat — conquering two worlds and practising Krishna consciousness simply.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:19 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada wrote a letter to one of his disciples. He came to India the first time. He came at this time in summer. who is suffering very difficult like you take a fish after water for some people some country is nine months cold nine months cold and then you take them out”

Maharaj sums up Prabhupada's letter in one word: tolerate. If you don't tolerate, you complicate the situation and suffer; tolerate, and soon it passes.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:04 (auto-transcript): “What is he saying? One word. Tolerate, thank you, tolerate it, right, tolerance is very important, anyone who doesn't want to suffer, tolerate, if you don't want to suffer, then don't tolerate, you complicate this situation. So tolerate. In a short while it will go away.”

children.topic: Equal to both — fit for liberation
children.note: The next Gita verse, 2.15, names who is eligible for liberation: not one who is always jolly, nor one who is always distressed, but one who is equal in both. Tolerate and you will transcend.

children.topic: It is the mind, not the soul
children.note:
Heat and cold, joy and distress come from the mind: the same water the mind calls too cold one day and too hot another. The soul is not touched.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:24 (auto-transcript): “the second thing is this heat and cold happiness and distress where is it coming from The mind is coming from the mind, not from the soul, it's from the mind, the same water, the same water, the mind says this is too cold, the mind says this is too hot, in the mind.”

Yogis sit naked in freezing water in the Himalayas, or amid fire, and keep chanting their mantras, having transcended the body. They were not born that way; it came by practice, and by practice we too can transcend dualities.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:16 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, you can see a yogi inside the pinching cold water. Go to Himalayas. People are sitting there naked. No dress. Naked. And they are able to chant their mantras. They can sit inside the fire. Naked. They should chant their mantras. Why? They have transcended the body.…”

Krishna asks us to tolerate because none of this is permanent. With tolerance life becomes simple; without it we are never satisfied, even in heaven. The satisfied person is the one who has conquered the mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:21 (auto-transcript): “so Krishna is requesting tolerate not permanent if he can tolerate life will become simple you can live in any situation and be satisfied if you cannot tolerate any way I will not be satisfied even if you go to heaven”

One who can tolerate can live anywhere and be content. — “you can live in any situation and be satisfied”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:43 (auto-transcript): “life will become simple you can live in any situation and be satisfied if you cannot tolerate any way I will not be satisfied even if you go to heaven you will not be satisfied One who is satisfied is one who has conquered the mind. But the discipline or tolerance we have…”

children.topic: One second saves a hundred years
children.note:
Why tolerate? Because it is temporary. One second of tolerance can save a person from a hundred years in prison.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:34 (auto-transcript): “Why should we tolerate it? Because it is temporary. One second, tolerance, one second, tolerance, and save us from 100 years in prison, one second, one second, 100 years in jail, so she tolerates. The other thing is that nothing is going to work according to our plan.”

Nothing goes according to our plans; even our perfect plans need Krishna's sanction, and without it they fail. So we must learn to tolerate.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:15 (auto-transcript): “The other thing is that nothing is going to work according to our plan. That's a famous quote. Man proposes, God disposes. all our perfect plans it depends on the sanction from Krishna Krishna does not sanction it”

Many people are better qualified than us yet lack our position, because Krishna must sanction it. In the First Canto, Prabhupada notes that Vidura's many blessings on Dhritarashtra were checked by Krishna: you do not merit this.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:30 (auto-transcript): “Just as, the positions which we have, there are many people who have the qualification better than us, that doesn't have it. Many people have better qualifications than what we have, and they don't have the position we have, because it has to be sanctioned by Krishna. Krishna…”

Knowledge matters because it shows us how to respond to every situation positively — not complicating issues but rectifying them. Transcending duality is our duty, possible by the Lord's mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:17 (auto-transcript): “Knowledge is important because he helps us to know how to respond to every situation in a positive way. We should not complicate our issue. It will be better to rectify the issue. That is the purpose of knowledge. Help us to deal with the situation that will bring all the…”

children.topic: Five minutes on a Lagos bridge
children.note:
Lagos traffic locks head to head every day because no one will wait — everyone wants to go first. If all waited and went slowly, traffic would keep moving. Lack of tolerance is the cause.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:31 (auto-transcript): “Practical experience. Why we should tolerate. Particularly. There was an incident in Nigeria. Lagos city, a lot of traffic. Heavy traffic. And you will see. Driving. If you want to prepare your driving work, go to Legos.”

children.topic: A slap over a rubber bumper
children.note:
A motorcyclist bumped a lady's car; the bumper was only rubber and nothing was damaged. She got out, shouted and slapped him; insulted, he grabbed her, they struggled, and she fell from the bridge and died. Five minutes — she lost her life, the car stayed behind, and he was arrested.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:24 (auto-transcript): “So this day, a lady, was on her car. Another man, was on her bike. Everybody is trying to find their way. By providence, the man hit the bomber of the car. Suddenly, he stopped the car. Came outside. She looked.”

When something goes wrong, what is our 'right' worth if we don't know how to apply it? Useless. So practise tolerance in every situation; the disciple is meant to learn these qualities and take them seriously in sadhana. — “Our right has no value.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:21 (auto-transcript): “So what is our right, when something has gone wrong, what is our right? Our right has no value. If you don't know how to apply it, useless. Therefore, You should practice to be taught in every situation. Then you will understand.”

Questions from the devotees, several carried over from the previous day's class.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:14 (auto-transcript): “when we were talking about situations where how we deal with a person is perceived by them. So whatever is inside, they will feel. Many a times there are certain kind of people who have a very disturbing nature or that is how they behave despite giving them corrections also.…”

children.topic: Q1 · Wrong to know people's natures?
children.note:
Since others feel what is inside us, is it harmful to hold a perception that certain people behave in a certain way?

🎙 Maharaj at 32:14 (auto-transcript): “when we were talking about situations where how we deal with a person is perceived by them. So whatever is inside, they will feel. Many a times there are certain kind of people who have a very disturbing nature or that is how they behave despite giving them corrections also.…”

It is good to know each other and what to expect from each person; otherwise we will have issues with everybody. The spiritual master, the king and the teacher especially must know their followers and deal with each according to their level.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:20 (auto-transcript): “It is good to know, we should know each other, so we should know what to expect from anyone. If we don't know that, we will constantly have an issue with everybody. Especially, the spiritual master, the king, the teacher, should know the followers.”

children.topic: The ticket to Goloka is here
children.note:
We want to go to Godhead, but the ticket is earned here: by understanding whom we are dealing with and learning to relate with everyone, we qualify to relate with Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:46 (auto-transcript): “We want to go to Godhead. For what? We want to go to Godhead. How will we get it? Are they getting Goloka? Are they getting Goloka? No, it is here, you have to get a ticket from here, by understanding who am I dealing with,”

Marriages fall apart because partners expect from each other what the other does not have — like going to a poor man for festival sponsorship. Underneath is selfishness: relating for my interest, not yours. That thought is a message the other person feels, and friction follows.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:09 (auto-transcript): “So many marriages are falling apart. Why? They don't understand each other. I'm expecting for me what you don't have. I'm expecting for me what I don't have. What would happen? Fight. can you imagine you have a festival to celebrate and you have gone to meet a poor person who…”

A saintly person does not get angry because he knows who is in ignorance, passion or goodness; he expects their behaviour, so it does not disturb him.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:34 (auto-transcript): “Why a saintly person does not get angry? Why? Because he knows that. He knows. He knows. This person is in ignorance, this person is in goodness, this person is in passion, they know. Whatever we do, it doesn't affect them. Because they're expecting it.”

children.topic: Don't expect a sudra to be a paramahamsa
children.note:
A devotee complained bitterly about another; Maharaj laughed until she stopped, then told her the problem was hers — she wanted a sudra to behave like a paramahamsa. By the fruit you know the tree. Ask a neophyte to help carry a computer and he may say: I came for Krishna, not for you.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:23 (auto-transcript): “What devotee was complaining. Very bitterly. Why does this devotee behave like this? So I was laughing when she was laughing. She was angry but I was laughing. So she stopped. And I said, do you know the problem? You are mistaking the sudra for a Paramahamsa. You want a sudra…”

children.topic: Q2 · How does tolerance become realised?
children.note:
We hear so much about tolerance, yet when the moment comes we don't practise it. How does it become realised?

🎙 Maharaj at 43:03 (auto-transcript): “Hey Krishna Maharaj, we hear so much about tolerance. But when it comes to practice, we sometimes follow thoughts. taught, so how can it become a realized, you know, it becomes a realization and a realized practice. So, Mataji is asking, Sita Rani Mataji is asking, that we…”

Understand why you should tolerate: if I react, I will suffer, so I withdraw. When we know what to expect, it becomes easy; the beauty of scripture is that it gives this knowledge. — “we study these scriptures to know how to act.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:40 (auto-transcript): “It begins from understanding, why should I tolerate, why is it important for me to tolerate, I can't react to everything. Why should I not react to this? Because I am going to suffer if I do that. Right? So since I don't want to suffer,”

children.topic: Q3 · How far should one tolerate?
children.note:
Prithviraj Chauhan spared Muhammad Ghori again and again, until Ghori defeated and killed him; recently people were killed for their religion. How far should non-violence and tolerance go?

🎙 Maharaj at 46:17 (auto-transcript): “Prithvirachohan. So he was attacked by Afghani ruler, Ghori. And he was attacked 17 times and because of his being non-violent he defeated him 17 times and he left him. And when he came the 18th time, he defeated him took control over the nation and he took him back to his…”

A ruler's duty is to protect the citizens. When someone kills others — demonic, not religious, activity — the king must respond. Keeping quiet then is not tolerance. — “it is laziness or foolishness”

🎙 Maharaj at 48:58 (auto-transcript): “Irula has the duty to protect the citizens. Therefore, when the king is seeing that someone is killing other people, which is demonic activity, not religious, it is not religious, it is demonic. the king should take charge of it the king should respond to it”

Caitanya Mahaprabhu taught the principle: when Nityananda was attacked, he took action immediately. One who has that duty and does not act is lazy.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:27 (auto-transcript): “Chaitanya Mahaprabhu taught us that principle. When he saw Nityananda was attacked, he didn't do that. When he saw Nityananda was attacked, he didn't do that. Immediately he took action. He has shown his own value. He also needs to do this work. If he doesn't do this, he is…”

children.topic: Q4 · Blessings on those who behave badly?
children.note:
If someone behaves poorly yet receives a blessing from a bona fide guru that this is their last life, how can that be?

🎙 Maharaj at 54:21 (auto-transcript): “So from today, Maharaj, you said, when you say that we should know how people are so it is better for us to understand and know also what to expect from them so when I see that people are not behaving nicely or whatever but at the same time I hear that they are getting…”

Do you know their background? If it is wonderful, the blessing will work; if not, it is like the blessings Krishna checked for Dhritarashtra. A person neophyte today may carry a great past and be elevated tomorrow.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:49 (auto-transcript): “Do you know their background? Yes, we are seeing there is still nothing they are doing, but do you know their background? It's very important. If their background is wonderful, that blessing would work that it would work if their background is wonderful that blessing would…”

When pure devotees visit we spend all our time with them and our usual reading and hearing is missed. How to strike a balance?

🎙 Maharaj at 57:38 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, many times you have said in today's class that you have said that a strong sign is a volume of practice. and previously also many times we have said that association with pure devotees is also the most important thing and it's the best blessing given by Krishna to…”

Maharaj calls it a miscalculation: there is plenty of time in the day. After japa, are you cooking for the guru 24 hours? No — we sleep or talk prajalpa after mangala-arati. Take full advantage of what is available and manage time well.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:14 (auto-transcript): “I think it is a miscalculation. Because we have a lot of time. In our schedule, we have a lot of time. For everything. If you are doing chapter from, let's say, 1 to 4.30, how many hours is that? so let's just say that you chant”
